question: Assume today is 2026-09-05. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of new passenger cars (Pkw) registered in Germany in September 2026, as it will be first reported in the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt's (KBA) monthly press release on vehicle registrations.

target.what: New passenger car (Pkw) registrations in Germany during September 2026, as first reported by the KBA monthly press release on vehicle registrations (Fahrzeugzulassungen). Counts newly registered passenger cars (Pkw) with German registration, including commercial and private, domestic registrations o
target.cadence: monthly press release (Fahrzeugzulassungen), typically published in the first days of the following month
target.caveats: Target period is future relative to cutoff (2026-09-05); only ~5 days of September are observable at cutoff. Working interpretation: total Pkw new registrations (all brands, all fuel types, private + commercial) for calendar September 2026, as first published. Alternatives: private-only vs total; Pk

candidates.hypothesis: September registrations follow a strong seasonal pattern; prior Septembers and recent monthly values (Jan-Aug 2026) anchor the level and seasonal multiplier. Target = recent run-rate × September seasonal factor.
candidates.data_to_find: KBA monthly Pkw new registration totals for September 2023, 2024, 2025 and monthly values Jan-Aug 2026 (or latest available before cutoff); September seasonal factor relative to adjacent months.

candidates.perspective: Industry association (VDA) and OEM monthly data
candidates.hypothesis: VDA domestic passenger car registrations and OEM Germany sales figures track KBA totals closely; they can proxy or cross-check the September level. Target ≈ VDA domestic registrations adjusted for coverage differences.
candidates.data_to_find: VDA monthly domestic Pkw registrations or Inlandsmarkt figures for 2026 months and September prior years; OEM (VW, Mercedes, BMW, Stellantis) Germany registration/sales commentary for September 2026.
search_hints: Germany passenger car registrations August 2026 VDA

candidates.hypothesis: Published 2026 German car market forecasts (full-year registrations) can be decomposed into monthly path; September share of annual total is historically stable (~9-10%). Target = annual forecast × September share.
candidates.data_to_find: Full-year 2026 Germany new passenger car registration forecasts (e.g., from industry bodies, banks, research firms) available before cutoff; historical September share of annual registrations.

candidates.hypothesis: EV subsidy changes, CO2 rules, interest rates, and consumer confidence shift the September level; identifiable policy deadlines (e.g., incentive expiry) can pull registrations forward or depress them. Quantify exposure.
candidates.data_to_find: German EV purchase incentive (Umweltbonus/company car tax) changes effective 2026; any registration-relevant policy deadlines around September 2026; consumer confidence and auto demand indicators mid-2026.
search_hints: Germany EV subsidy 2026 changes car registrations

candidates.hypothesis: Dealer order intake and delivery backlogs lead registrations by weeks; strong order books in mid-2026 imply higher September registrations. Target constrained by deliveries scheduled in September.
candidates.data_to_find: German dealer order intake / order backlog indicators (e.g., ifo auto industry orders, KBA commercial registrations), delivery lead times mid-2026.

candidates.hypothesis: September is a high month due to new registration plate cycle and quarter-end; the September-to-August ratio and September share of annual total are stable base rates. Target = August 2026 actual × September/August ratio.
candidates.data_to_find: Historical September/August registration ratios and September share of annual Pkw registrations (2015-2025); August 2026 actual registrations if published before cutoff.
search_hints: September August ratio car registrations Germany seasonal

p57.role: August 2026 total Pkw new registrations in Germany (KBA)

methods.rationale: Anchors on the most recent observed KBA month (August 2026, 212,563) and applies a September/August seasonal ratio derived from kept historical pairs (2015-2017, 2025), excluding WLTP-distorted 2018/2019. Shared dependency: both the August level and the ratio come from KBA data; failure mode is an unusual September policy or macro shock.

p144.role: VDA full-year 2026 Germany Pkw new registration forecast (2.9mn)

methods.rationale: Decomposes the VDA 2.9mn annual forecast into a September level via a historically stable September share. Shared dependency: relies on the VDA forecast being realised; failure mode is a forecast miss or a September share outside the historical band. Cross-checks the August-anchored route.

Scales last September's KBA total (235,528) by the year-on-year movement in the August KBA total (212,563 vs August 2025 ~207,229, i.e. +2.6%). This uses the observed August 2026 y/y growth as a proxy for September y/y growth. Shared dependency: assumes September y/y growth tracks August y/y growth; failure mode is a September-specific shock (subsidy pull, plate cycle) that breaks the month-to-month growth link.

assumptions.name: September/August seasonal ratio 2026
assumptions.rationale: Historical September/August ratios from kept pairs: 2015 1.20, 2016 1.22, 2017 1.13, 2018 0.63 (WLTP-distorted), 2019 0.78 (WLTP-distorted), 2025 1.137 (p1/p31). Excluding WLTP years, ratios cluster 1.13-1.22; 2026 has a strong EV-subsidy pull that may lift September, but also a weaker overall market, so a central 1.12 with wide range is reasonable.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 follows a normal plate-cycle/quarter-end pattern without a major policy deadline distortion.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a September 2026 policy deadline (e.g. subsidy change) that pulls registrations forward or depresses them, or a September/August ratio outside 1.0-1.25 in comparable non-WLTP years.

assumptions.name: September share of full-year 2026 registrations
assumptions.rationale: September is historically a high month; in 2025 September 235,528 was ~11.2% of the ~2.1mn Jan-Sep run-rate annualised, and September typically accounts for roughly 8.5-9.5% of the annual total. Using the VDA 2.9mn forecast, a ~8.8% share gives a September level consistent with the August-anchored route.
assumptions.applies_when: The VDA 2.9mn full-year forecast is broadly realised and September's seasonal share is near its historical norm.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that 2026 monthly path deviates strongly from the annual forecast (e.g. H2 collapse or boom), or a September share outside 7.8-9.8% in comparable years.

p628.role: August 2026 total Pkw new registrations in Germany (KBA), 212,563

methods.rationale: Base-rate route: August 2026 actual (p628, the VDA/KBA table value 212,563) times a September/August seasonal ratio. September is typically above August due to the new plate cycle and quarter-end; 2025 showed +13.7%. The ratio assumption is the main uncertainty; the August level is well observed. Repaired: p57 replaced by p628, which carries the exact 212,563 figure the role requires.

p144.role: VDA full-year 2026 Germany Pkw new registration forecast (2.9mn)

methods.rationale: Forecast-decomposition route: VDA full-year 2026 forecast (p144, corroborated by p167/p181/p205) times September's share of the annual total. September share is historically ~9%; the assumption carries the seasonal and realisation uncertainty. Shared dependency: relies on the VDA forecast being realised.

p1.role: September 2025 total Pkw new registrations in Germany (KBA), 235,528

methods.rationale: Year-on-year route: September 2025 actual (p1) scaled by a September 2026 y/y growth factor. Replaces the failed yoy_scaling (which needed an August 2025 signal not in the kept data) with a formula_mc using an explicit growth assumption. The assumption is anchored on August 2026 +2.6% y/y (p281/p628) and Jan-Aug 2026 +5% cumulative (p628), tempered by the strong September 2025 base (+12.8%, p3).

assumptions.name: September/August seasonal ratio for 2026
assumptions.rationale: September 2025 was +13.7% vs August 2025 (p2/p32/p113); September 2023 was -17.9% vs August 2023 (p516) but that August was distorted by the EV subsidy pull-forward. Non-distorted years (2015-2017) show September above August. A ratio near 1.10-1.15 is typical; 2026 has a new EV incentive supporting September. Range spans weak (1.0) to strong (1.25) seasonality.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 follows a normal plate-cycle/quarter-end pattern without a major pull-forward or policy cliff.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a September 2026 policy deadline pulling registrations into August, or a collapse in order books.

assumptions.name: September share of full-year 2026 registrations
assumptions.rationale: September is historically a high month; September 2025 (235,528) was about 11% of the ~2.1mn Jan-Sep 2025 cumulative, implying a September share of the full year near 9%. Using 8.8% with a range 7.8-9.8% reflects month-to-month variation and the possibility that the annual total is not evenly distributed.
assumptions.applies_when: The VDA 2.9mn full-year forecast is broadly realised and September's share of the year is near its historical average.
assumptions.falsified_by: A September share materially outside 7.8-9.8% in comparable years, or a large deviation of the annual total from 2.9mn.

assumptions.name: September 2026 / September 2025 year-on-year growth factor
assumptions.rationale: Used to scale September 2025 (p1) to September 2026. August 2026 was +2.6% y/y (p281/p628) and Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative was +5% (p628), so the current-year run-rate is modestly above 2025. September 2025 was itself +12.8% y/y (p3), an unusually strong base, so the 2026 y/y growth for September is likely lower than the August pace. A factor near 1.0 with a 0.9-1.1 range reflects this offsetting pattern.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 y/y growth is close to the recent run-rate, without a policy cliff or pull-forward.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 y/y growth is far outside 0.9-1.1 relative to September 2025.

p628.role: August 2026 total Pkw new registrations in Germany (KBA), 212,563

previous_methods.rationale: Base-rate route: August 2026 actual (p628, the VDA/KBA table value 212,563) times a September/August seasonal ratio. September is typically above August due to the new plate cycle and quarter-end; 2025 showed +13.7%. The ratio assumption is the main uncertainty; the August level is well observed. Repaired: p57 replaced by p628, which carries the exact 212,563 figure the role requires.

p144.role: VDA full-year 2026 Germany Pkw new registration forecast (2.9mn)

previous_methods.rationale: Forecast-decomposition route: VDA full-year 2026 forecast (p144, corroborated by p167/p181/p205) times September's share of the annual total. September share is historically ~9%; the assumption carries the seasonal and realisation uncertainty. Shared dependency: relies on the VDA forecast being realised.

p1.role: September 2025 total Pkw new registrations in Germany (KBA), 235,528

previous_methods.rationale: Year-on-year route: September 2025 actual (p1) scaled by a September 2026 y/y growth factor. Replaces the failed yoy_scaling (which needed an August 2025 signal not in the kept data) with a formula_mc using an explicit growth assumption. The assumption is anchored on August 2026 +2.6% y/y (p281/p628) and Jan-Aug 2026 +5% cumulative (p628), tempered by the strong September 2025 base (+12.8%, p3).

previous_assumptions.name: September/August seasonal ratio for 2026
previous_assumptions.rationale: September 2025 was +13.7% vs August 2025 (p2/p32/p113); September 2023 was -17.9% vs August 2023 (p516) but that August was distorted by the EV subsidy pull-forward. Non-distorted years (2015-2017) show September above August. A ratio near 1.10-1.15 is typical; 2026 has a new EV incentive supporting September. Range spans weak (1.0) to strong (1.25) seasonality.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 follows a normal plate-cycle/quarter-end pattern without a major pull-forward or policy cliff.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a September 2026 policy deadline pulling registrations into August, or a collapse in order books.

previous_assumptions.name: September share of full-year 2026 registrations
previous_assumptions.rationale: September is historically a high month; September 2025 (235,528) was about 11% of the ~2.1mn Jan-Sep 2025 cumulative, implying a September share of the full year near 9%. Using 8.8% with a range 7.8-9.8% reflects month-to-month variation and the possibility that the annual total is not evenly distributed.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: The VDA 2.9mn full-year forecast is broadly realised and September's share of the year is near its historical average.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: A September share materially outside 7.8-9.8% in comparable years, or a large deviation of the annual total from 2.9mn.

previous_assumptions.name: September 2026 / September 2025 year-on-year growth factor
previous_assumptions.rationale: Used to scale September 2025 (p1) to September 2026. August 2026 was +2.6% y/y (p281/p628) and Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative was +5% (p628), so the current-year run-rate is modestly above 2025. September 2025 was itself +12.8% y/y (p3), an unusually strong base, so the 2026 y/y growth for September is likely lower than the August pace. A factor near 1.0 with a 0.9-1.1 range reflects this offsetting pattern.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 y/y growth is close to the recent run-rate, without a policy cliff or pull-forward.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 y/y growth is far outside 0.9-1.1 relative to September 2025.

methods.label: m2

p144.role: VDA full-year 2026 Germany Pkw new registration forecast (2.9mn)

methods.rationale: Forecast-decomposition route: VDA full-year 2026 forecast (p144, corroborated by p167/p181/p205) times September's share of the annual total. September share is historically ~9%; the assumption carries the seasonal and realisation uncertainty. Shared dependency: relies on the VDA forecast being realised.

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

interval.rule: one block, so the interval is that block's own width

excluded_by_input_audit.reason: input audit: p628: The evidence value is 213 new passenger car registrations for August 2026, not the stated 212,563 total; the quantity is a different magnitude than the role requires.

excluded_by_input_audit.label: m3
excluded_by_input_audit.reason: input audit: p1: The evidence value is 236 new passenger car registrations for September 2025, not the stated 235,528; the quantity is a different magnitude than the role requires.

kept.name: September/August seasonal ratio for 2026
kept.rationale: September 2025 was +13.7% vs August 2025 (p2/p32/p113); September 2023 was -17.9% vs August 2023 (p516) but that August was distorted by the EV subsidy pull-forward. Non-distorted years (2015-2017) show September above August. A ratio near 1.10-1.15 is typical; 2026 has a new EV incentive supporting
kept.applies_when: September 2026 follows a normal plate-cycle/quarter-end pattern without a major pull-forward or policy cliff.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a September 2026 policy deadline pulling registrations into August, or a collapse in order books.

kept.name: September share of full-year 2026 registrations
kept.rationale: September is historically a high month; September 2025 (235,528) was about 11% of the ~2.1mn Jan-Sep 2025 cumulative, implying a September share of the full year near 9%. Using 8.8% with a range 7.8-9.8% reflects month-to-month variation and the possibility that the annual total is not evenly distri
kept.applies_when: The VDA 2.9mn full-year forecast is broadly realised and September's share of the year is near its historical average.
kept.falsified_by: A September share materially outside 7.8-9.8% in comparable years, or a large deviation of the annual total from 2.9mn.

kept.name: September 2026 / September 2025 year-on-year growth factor
kept.rationale: Used to scale September 2025 (p1) to September 2026. August 2026 was +2.6% y/y (p281/p628) and Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative was +5% (p628), so the current-year run-rate is modestly above 2025. September 2025 was itself +12.8% y/y (p3), an unusually strong base, so the 2026 y/y growth for September is lik
kept.applies_when: September 2026 y/y growth is close to the recent run-rate, without a policy cliff or pull-forward.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 y/y growth is far outside 0.9-1.1 relative to September 2025.

Method: the only block multiplies the VDA full-year 2026 forecast of [[p144_value]] by an assumed September share of [[a2_value]] (range [[a2_low]] to [[a2_high]]). by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
